text: This lab puts the chapter together end to end: starting from a qubit state, you'll compute measurement probabilities, turn those probabilities into expected shot counts for a real experiment, and plot the result as a histogram-style bar chart, the exact plot you'll see in the output of almost every real quantum circuit run.

A real quantum device doesn't report probabilities directly, it reports a count of how many times each outcome occurred across N repeated measurements, called shots. The expected count for an outcome is N times its probability, exact arithmetic, the long-run average, not a guarantee about any single run. A real device might still report numbers slightly off from that, purely from statistical noise. The chart's y-axis is a count, not a probability, and labeling it correctly matters. And wrapping the whole pattern in one reusable function handles any normalized probability list and shot count.

For P-zero equals point two five and P-one equals point seven five, after confirming they sum to one, a thousand shots gives expected counts of exactly two hundred fifty and seven hundred fifty. Treat that as the theoretical expectation — a real device measuring this exact state a thousand times might report two hundred forty-three and seven hundred fifty-seven, the same kind of fluctuation as a fair coin not landing exactly five hundred-five hundred in a thousand flips.

Since you'll build this exact plot repeatedly throughout the rest of this course, wrapping it in a function once pays off. plot_expected_counts asserts the probabilities sum to one, multiplies each by n_shots, and bars the result. For probabilities point one and point nine with five hundred shots, it hands back expected counts of fifty and four hundred fifty — the same function handles single-qubit or multi-qubit outcome sets identically.
Chapter 5 shifts from visualization to workflow: random seeds and reproducible simulation, the scientific-computing habits that make a result trustworthy and repeatable for the rest of this course.
